basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 16.' and it opens 'Vers. 16. Et tu insidiaberis calcaneo ejus. In calcaneo finis est corporis. Calcaneo ergo'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 16. Et tu insidiaberis calcaneo ejus. In calcaneo finis est corporis. Calcaneo ergo diabolus insidiatur, quia maxime in fine vult homines decipere. | Mulieri quoque dixit: Multiplicabo aerumnas tuas, in dolore paries filios. Quia illa, si non peccasset, sine dolore paritura erat: idcirco post peccatum ei haec poena irrogatur, ut in dolore pariat jam filios. Et sub viri potestate eris, et ipse dominabitur tui. Etiamsi non peccasset, sub potestate viri futura erat. Sed illa subjectio minus poenalis esset, quia ex dilectione procederet quae nunc ei pro poena imponitur ut etiam nolens viro subdatur. Moraliter sub potestate viri mulier constituitur: quia spiritui caro subdenda est, ne repugnet, sed magis obtemperet.
